subject.title: fix(qqbot): allow approval buttons in direct C2C conversations

question: Which identity is authoritative for fallback approval buttons in a QQBot C2C conversation when execApprovals is absent and DM access is open?
rationale: Source and documentation establish that a direct conversation is not itself proof of owner identity, but choosing between explicit configuration and a new originating-actor binding changes the product security contract.

options.title: Keep Explicit Authority
options.body: Require a non-wildcard allowFrom or configured execApprovals approver and document the configuration needed for the reported workflow.

options.title: Bind The Originating Actor
options.body: Add a narrowly specified identity binding between the approval request initiator and callback sender, with replay and attacker-denial coverage.

options.title: Trust Every C2C Sender
options.body: Accept direct-conversation membership as approval authority and explicitly own the broader open-DM security exposure.

recommendation.title: Keep Explicit Authority
recommendation.body: Require a non-wildcard allowFrom or configured execApprovals approver and document the configuration needed for the reported workflow.

likelyOwner.reason: Reviewed and merged the existing authorization boundary and is the strongest available decision owner for changing that contract.
